title: Nov 21 update: round-1 seeds, base share, offset G0, push direction
question: Is the small chains' round-1 drop seed noise or real; does base share fix it; do end-effector offsets create choices worth ranking; does round 1 re-apply round 0's push?
verdict: b100's drop was training-seed variance (seed 1 77.0 vs 53.0); b50cv drops with both seeds; mt100cv seed 1 holds on task 64 (73.3) but collapses on moka. 91% base frames rescues val only. Offset G0 passes (+12 points best-of-8). Round-1 pushes are not more aligned with r0 where they drop. Correction: mt100cv r1 moka val is 32.1%, not 4.5% (errored eval).
